name: cyclin dependent kinase 8
pathways: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

function.text: CDK8 encodes cyclin-dependent kinase 8. Annotated molecular activities include protein kinase activity and protein serine kinase activity. It participates in positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to intellectual developmental disorder with hypotonia and behavioral abnormalities (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: CDK8 amplification and increased activity have been described in colorectal cancer, with experimental evidence linking CDK8 to beta-catenin-dependent tumor-cell proliferation. This amplification-associated context is distinct from an isolated sequence variant.

function.text: CDK8 encodes cyclin-dependent kinase 8. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the Mediator complex, a coactivator involved in regulated gene transcription of nearly all RNA polymerase II-dependent genes. Mediator is recruited to promoters by direct interactions with regulatory proteins and serves as a scaffold for the assembly of a functional pre-initiation complex with RNA polymerase II and the general transcription factors. It phosphorylates the CTD (C-terminal domain) of the large subunit of RNA polymerase II (RNAp II), which may inhibit the formation of a transcription initiation complex.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with intellectual developmental disorder with hypotonia and behavioral abnormalities (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: CDK8 amplification and increased activity have been described in colorectal cancer, with experimental evidence linking CDK8 to beta-catenin-dependent tumor-cell proliferation. This amplification-associated context is distinct from an isolated sequence variant.
